rules.claim_phrases: SUPERSEDED by rules.verbatim for every item with fact_phrases (copy a claim phrase verbatim, as its own sentence). Older items: ALLOWLIST (HQ 2026-10-19): any sentence of a post that compares, ranks or orders anything - best / worst / biggest / largest / most / least / top / led / #N / first / second / next / then / followed by / only / all / every / none / record / ever / since / streak / in a row / again / double / twice / half / N times / more than / less than / any '-er than' / beat / missed / outperformed / lagged / winner / loser / last / bottom, and every other word like them - must be one of the item's claim_phrases, copied verbatim as its own sentence (only 'and' / 'also' / 'so' / 'plus' may stand around it). No claim phrase for what you want to say = say it without comparing (plain numbers from allowed_numbers). The facts_text describes the data; it is not a phrase list. A question to the reader that names no company, sector or number is exempt ('Which move surprised you most?')
rules.plain_words: SUPERSEDED by rules.verbatim for every item with fact_phrases (no free-form factual sentence at all). Older items: ROUND 2 (HQ 2026-10-19): every sentence that is not a claim phrase uses only plain words: the item's cashtags, company / person names and sectors, its allowed numbers and dates, its window ('on Friday', 'in the week to Oct 16', 'last week' for a week item), 'the 500 largest US-listed stocks', and a closed list of plain words (reported, filed, bought, sold, moved, rose, fell, gained, lost, dropped, declined, up, down, closed, market value, earnings, revenue, EPS, consensus, open-market, Form 4, picks, link in bio, ...). Any other word - a synonym of best / only ('alone', 'just', 'the one', 'the rest', 'other', 'exception', 'took gold', 'star'), an order or table word, a streak word ('kept', 'continued', 'extended', 'another', 'deepened'), an equality word ('same', 'matched', 'equaled'), an intensity verb ('surged', 'tanked', 'sold off', 'in the green', 'higher', 'lower'), a number word ('three'), a month ('in October'), 'every' / 'all' / 'each', an arrow / medal emoji, or > < = - makes the sentence need to be a claim phrase verbatim. Numbers and moves are tied to their subject: each number goes right after the company / sector it belongs to ('$MSFT −1.13%', never '$MSFT +2.03%' when +2.03% is $AAPL's), and rose / fell / up / down must match the move of every company / sector it is said of (never a move the item does not give, never negated, never with will / could / may).
rules.claims: superseded by claim_phrases (kept for the direction / date reading): comparatives and superlatives (led, biggest, largest, worst, best, most, least, only, first, top, #1, record, 'outperformed every other') only as the item's claims state them: name only that claim's companies / sectors in that sentence; each claim has a polarity (best = top gainer, worst = top loser, null = no side) and a rank (1 = its one subject is #1; group = its subjects are the top N in order) and a metric (usd_change, pct_change, market_cap, ...): say the side with the noun ('top loser', 'led the drop', 'biggest gainer'; 'top' / 'led' / '#1' alone or with an entity noun ('top sector', 'led its sector') read as best, whatever number stands beside them; with any other noun ('led the rout', 'top casualty') say best / worst instead), say the metric as the claim does (dollars vs percent vs market cap), the singular ('the biggest drop') only for the rank-1 subject, a list only from #1 in order, 'among the biggest' for other members, 'the two biggest' / 'one of the two biggest' only for the top 2; '#N by <metric>' only as the item's rank_by_usd / rank_by_cap / claims state it; 'of the 500' / 'overall' / 'of all' / 'on the day' only with a claim that has no within, 'of the 10' for the basket; a sector only as a sector claim (kind sector) says, a stock 'within' a sector only with that sector next to the word ('in Tech', 'Tech's', 'its sector'); a company named in words (Microsoft) counts as its cashtag; a sentence that names no company ('It was the biggest...', 'The biggest dollar drop of the 500.') is about the one named before it; 'too' / 'so was X' after a superlative adds X to it; a question is checked like a statement (only one about the reader, naming nothing, is exempt); 'did better than' / 'outperformed' / 'fell more than' compare percent unless dollars are named, and need a claim of that metric; never widen the window ('ever', 'in months', 'of the quarter', 'since September', a week on a one-session item) or call the session 'today' / 'yesterday' / 'this morning' / 'pre-market' / another weekday unless the item's when does; rules.moves: each item's moves: numbers = the sign of every number it allows with one sign, subjects = the direction of every company / sector it describes; never put a gain word (rose, gained, up) beside a loss or a loss word beside a gain ('Energy fell 2.6%' when Energy rose)
